lines.trans: What a mix-up! Let me look at the tag with my glasses.
Does it have a name or a phone number?
Unfortunately there is no phone number. Only two initials and an old street.
Wait a moment, that street is right here in our neighbourhood, five minutes away!
How strange! We rode the same morning train to the same neighbourhood.
Clara, call the station lost-and-found office right away.
I am dialling right now... Hello? Is anyone looking for a swapped blue suitcase?
Tell them mine has a red ribbon in the top pocket!
Not yet? Please write down our phone number and our address. Thank you!
They know nothing yet, madam, I am terribly sorry.
It is not your fault. Still, I only have the coat on my back!

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: Wait one second: Rocio is waving to me from the cafe with an idea!
See you soon!

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.
How is everything going this morning?

meanings.note: ¡Vaya lío! = What a mess!

examples.trans: The mess is here.

examples.text: Vemos los líos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the messs from the door.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.
Let me help you with that box.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Luggage tag or bottle label.

examples.trans: The tag is here.

examples.text: Vemos las etiquetas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tags from the door.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: Plural-only feminine noun in Spain: las gafas.

examples.trans: Where did I leave my glasses?
He wears round glasses.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Shortens to algún before masculine singular nouns (algún problema).

examples.trans: Does it have any sign on the door?
I bought some red apples.

meanings.note: Nombre y apellidos = full name.

examples.trans: The name is here.

examples.text: Vemos los nombres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the names from the door.

meanings.note: Becomes u before words starting with o- or ho-.

examples.trans: Do you prefer coffee or hot tea?
Do we open today or wait until tomorrow?

meanings.note: Written after street names in Spanish addresses (Calle Mayor número ocho).

examples.trans: The number is here.

examples.text: Vemos los números desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the numbers from the door.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Por teléfono = by phone / on the phone.

examples.trans: The telephone is here.

examples.text: Vemos los teléfonos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the telephones from the door.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Por desgracia = unfortunately.

examples.text: La desgracia es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The misfortune is very important here.
We talk about the misfortune.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.
We have already prepared the rooms.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.
Only a single room remains vacant.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Plural las iniciales.

examples.trans: The initial is here.

examples.text: Vemos las iniciales desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the initials from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.trans: The street is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the streets from the door.

meanings.note: Placed after a noun, means 'historic' or 'old-fashioned'.

examples.trans: It is an old piece.

examples.text: Encantada, Tomás, ¡siempre que nadie hable de vender pianos antiguos!
examples.trans: Gladly, Tomas, as long as nobody talks about selling old pianos!

meanings.note: De momento = for now.

examples.trans: The moment is here.

examples.text: Vemos los momentos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the moments from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.
Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Local city district with its own shops and squares.

examples.trans: The neighbourhood is here.

examples.text: Vemos los barrios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the neighbourhoods from the door.

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Faltan cinco minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is five minutes to twelve.

examples.text: Tenemos cinco mesas en el patio.
examples.trans: We have five tables in the courtyard.

meanings.note: En cinco minutos = in five minutes.

examples.trans: The minute is here.

examples.text: Vemos los minutos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the minutes from the door.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

meanings.note: ¡Qué extraño! = How strange!

examples.trans: It is a strange piece.

examples.text: ¡Qué extraño! Viajamos en el mismo tren de la mañana al mismo barrio.
examples.trans: How strange! We rode the same morning train to the same neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Siempre viajo en tren junto a la ventana.
examples.trans: I always travel by train next to the window.

examples.text: Viajamos a Valencia el lunes por la mañana.
examples.trans: We travelled to Valencia on Monday morning.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.
In ahora mismo, meaning right now, mismo strengthens the time word ahora. Now comes from ahora; mismo supplies emphasis without agreeing with a person in this expression.

examples.trans: We have the same job.
I am busy right now.

meanings.note: Plural los trenes.

examples.trans: The train is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trenes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the trains from the door.

meanings.note: La mañana = the morning; mañana (without article) = tomorrow.

examples.text: Por la mañana servimos café caliente.
examples.trans: In the morning we serve hot coffee.
See you tomorrow at eight!

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

llamar.gloss: to call; to ring; to be named (llamarse)

meanings.en: to call; to ring; to be named (llamarse)
meanings.note: ¿Cómo se llama? asks someone's name.

examples.trans: I am from here, pleased to meet you.
Someone called by phone yesterday.

meanings.note: Written as one word in modern Spanish.

examples.trans: I will bring breakfast up right away.
I will be right back with the key.

meanings.note: Objetos perdidos is the standard Spanish phrase for lost-and-found.

examples.trans: The object is here.

examples.text: Vemos los objetos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the objects from the door.

meanings.note: Objetos perdidos = lost property.

examples.trans: It is a lost piece.

examples.text: Clara, llama enseguida a objetos perdidos de la estación.
examples.trans: Clara, call the station lost-and-found office right away.

meanings.note: La estación de tren = the train station.

examples.trans: The station is here.

examples.text: Vemos las estaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stations from the door.

marcar.gloss: to show (the time); to dial; to mark

meanings.en: to show (the time); to dial; to mark
meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells c -> qu: marqué.

examples.text: El reloj de la torre marca las doce.
examples.trans: The tower clock shows twelve.

examples.text: Marqué el número de la estación.
examples.trans: I dialled the station number.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.trans: I am heading there right now.
Now we have four free tables.

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.
Of course, come right in!

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?
Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Refers exclusively to people.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de llamar a la puerta.
examples.trans: Someone just knocked at the door.
Is anyone at the front desk?

buscar.gloss: to look for; to search for

meanings.en: to look for; to search for
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'for' (busco la llave = I am looking for the key).

examples.trans: I am looking for the blue door.

examples.text: Ayer busqué mis gafas por toda la casa.
examples.trans: Yesterday I looked for my glasses all over the house.

meanings.note: Hacer la maleta = to pack one's suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en la maleta.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in the suitcase.

meanings.note: Plural azules; azul marino means 'navy blue'.

examples.trans: It is a blue piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from cambiar.

examples.trans: It is a swapped piece.

examples.text: Marco ahora mismo... ¿Sí, dígame? ¿Alguien busca una maleta azul cambiada?
examples.trans: I am dialling right now... Hello? Is anyone looking for a swapped blue suitcase?

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

meanings.note: Stressed possessive (el mío, la mía, los míos, las mías); ¡Madre mía! = Goodness me!

examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

examples.text: Un amigo mío vive en esta calle.
examples.trans: A friend of mine lives on this street.

meanings.note: Silk ribbon or adhesive tape.

examples.trans: The ribbon is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cintas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ribbons from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number.

examples.trans: It is a red piece.

examples.text: ¡Dígales que la mía tiene una cinta roja en el bolsillo de arriba!
examples.trans: Tell them mine has a red ribbon in the top pocket!

meanings.note: Coat or trouser pocket.

examples.trans: The pocket is here.

examples.text: Vemos los bolsillos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pockets from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of abajo.

examples.trans: The bedrooms are upstairs.
Look up toward the balcony.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'still' or 'not yet'.

examples.trans: The coffee is still hot.
It is not twelve o'clock yet.

anotar.gloss: to note down; to write down

meanings.en: to note down; to write down
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Anoto el teléfono en mi cuaderno.
examples.trans: I write the phone number in my notebook.
The receptionist noted down the time.

meanings.note: Plural direcciones.

examples.trans: The address is here.

examples.text: Vemos las direcciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the addresss from the door.

meanings.note: Por favor literally means 'as a favour'.

examples.trans: The favour is here.

examples.text: Vemos los favores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the favours from the door.

meanings.note: Gracias por + noun/infinitive expresses 'thank you for...'.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your help!
Thank you for coming today.

saber.gloss: to know (a fact / how to); to taste (saber a)

meanings.en: to know (a fact / how to); to taste (saber a)
meanings.note: Irregular: sé, supe; sabe igual que = it tastes just like.

examples.trans: Do you know where the wrench is?

examples.text: Este bizcocho sabe a limón fresco.
examples.trans: This cake tastes of fresh lemon.

nada.gloss: nothing; not at all (de nada = you're welcome)

meanings.en: nothing; not at all (de nada = you're welcome)
meanings.note: No pasa nada = no problem; nada de... = no ... at all.

examples.trans: Easy now, there is no problem at all.
There is no butter left at all.

meanings.note: Polite form of address: señora Carmen.

examples.trans: The madam is here.

examples.text: Vemos las señoras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the madams from the door.

lo.gloss: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)

meanings.en: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)
meanings.note: Direct object pronoun before verbs (lo veo), and neuter article in lo que ('what') or lo mejor ('the best').

examples.text: Ya lo veo encima del estante.
examples.trans: I see it now on the shelf.

examples.text: Lo mejor del patio es la calma.
examples.trans: The best part of the courtyard is the calm.

sentir.gloss: to feel; to be sorry (lo siento)

meanings.en: to feel; to be sorry (lo siento)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie in present, e -> i in preterite 3rd: sintió).

examples.text: Lo siento mucho por la espera.
examples.trans: I am very sorry about the wait.

examples.text: Aquí cada huésped se siente en casa.
examples.trans: Here every guest feels at home.

meanings.note: Superlative degree of mucho.

examples.trans: I am terribly sorry, madam.
I am so happy for you.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Por nuestra culpa = because of us; no es culpa suya = it is not your fault.

examples.trans: The fault is here.

examples.text: Vemos las culpas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the faults from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: suyo, suya, suyos, suyas.

examples.trans: The courtyard is all yours.
Do not worry, it is not your fault.

meanings.note: Unaccented aun means 'even' (aun así = even so), distinct from aún (still/yet).

examples.text: Aun con lluvia, el patio es bonito.
examples.trans: Even in the rain, the courtyard is pretty.
Even so, we arrived on time.

meanings.note: Así que means 'so / therefore'.

examples.trans: Do it like this, slowly.
It is raining hard, so let us go inside.

meanings.note: Warm outer coat worn in cold or rainy weather.

examples.trans: The coat is here.

examples.text: Vemos los abrigos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the coats from the door.

meanings.note: Puesto de flores = flower stall.

examples.trans: The market stall is here.

examples.text: Vemos los puestos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the market stalls from the door.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.
We hope you rest very well.

meanings.note: Also a masculine noun (un segundo = one second).

examples.trans: It is a second piece.

examples.text: Segunda: Te he echado de menos estos tres años.
examples.trans: Second: I missed you these three years.

meanings.note: First-person singular object/reflexive pronoun.

examples.trans: Can you pass me the salt, please?
I live here and I work here.

hacer.gloss: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)

meanings.en: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)
meanings.note: Irregular: hago, hice, hecho; hace tres años = three years ago.

examples.text: La panadera hace pan fresco cada mañana.
examples.trans: The baker bakes fresh bread every morning.
She arrived ten minutes ago.

meanings.note: Hacer señas = to wave / motion to someone.

examples.trans: The wave is here.

examples.text: Vemos las señas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the waves from the door.

meanings.note: Marks a starting point in space or time.

examples.trans: We have not spoken since that Sunday.
We open to the public starting tomorrow.

meanings.note: Neighbourhood cafe serving coffee, tea, toast, and pastries.

examples.trans: The cafe is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cafeterías desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cafes from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Buena idea! = Good idea!

examples.trans: The idea is here.

examples.text: Vemos las ideas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ideas from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta pronto! = See you soon!

examples.trans: See you soon and safe travels!

examples.text: Esta mañana me desperté muy pronto.
examples.trans: This morning I woke up very early.
